issues.title: [Bug] Continuity textures fail to stitch / Resource Pack Format 97 mismatch on macOS (Minecraft 26.3)
issues.body:
After updating to the Minecraft 26.3 Wilderness Bound release on an M2 MacBook Pro via the Modrinth App, Continuity completely fails to render connected textures (specifically glass panes and blocks).
The game automatically pushes the built-in Continuity assets into the incompatibleResourcePacks category within options.txt upon boot. Manually stripping the string from the configuration file does not resolve the issue, as the game client forces the incompatibility lines back into the text block on the subsequent launch sequence.
This issue is occurring on a live Minecraft Realm where other players running Windows architectures are experiencing normal asset scaling and functional texture stitching.

Steps to Reproduce:
    1    Launch Minecraft 26.3 (Fabric / Modrinth Instance) on macOS (Apple Silicon M2).
    2    Connect to a 26.3 multiplayer Realm or local world.
    3    Open Options > Resource Packs and observe the Continuity core files flagged with format errors.
    4    Place glass panes or blocks; texture borders remain completely disconnected.

System Information:
    •    OS: macOS (Apple Silicon Architecture)
    •    Hardware: M2 MacBook Pro
    •    Game Version: Minecraft 26.3 (Wilderness Bound Update)
    •    Resource Pack Format Version: Format 97

    •    Mod Loader: Fabric
    •    Launcher: Modrinth App
    •    Active Mods: Iris Shaders, Sodium, Continuity (26.3 build variants)

issues.title: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in Sodium's LevelSlice.getBlockState, triggered via Continuity's StandardOverlayQuadProcessor.getEmitter — possible bit-shift bug with negative section Y
issues.body:
**Environment**
- Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248
- Sodium 0.8.12+mc1.21.1
- Continuity 3.0.0+1.21.neoforge
- Iris 1.8.14-beta.1

I've hit this crash three times so far, always during chunk mesh building, always on `minecraft:deepslate` level.


**Possible pattern in the corrupted index (unconfirmed, just a hypothesis)**
The three crashes I've collected all produced indices that look like clean multiples of 2^21 (2097152) plus a small remainder that would otherwise be a valid array index (0–26, since the LevelSlice cache is a 3×3×3 = 27 array):

| Crash | Index | ≈ Fit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | -2097139 | -(1 × 2^21) + 13 |
| 2 | -2097140 | -(1 × 2^21) + 12 |
| 3 | -6291443 | -(3 × 2^21) + 13 |

I don't know exacly what this means but it seems like during the neighbor serch a cordinate  is being shifted by 21 bits. Since section Y can be negative near bedrock/deep-slate layers, that could produce these large negative indices instead I want to stress this is just a hypothesis from pattern-matching three data points.

**Repro conditions (best guess)**
- Happens specifically while rendering `deepslate` sections
- All three crashes were around y=-64 to y=-17

issues.title: Continuity does not support/call NeoForge's `BakedModel.getRenderPasses`
issues.body:
NeoForge provides a method [`BakedModel.getRenderPasses(ItemStack, ...)`](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/d8d64b44bb46323d44520fe27feda0a9a08c1c82/src/main/java/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/extensions/IBakedModelExtension.java#L110-L112) method, which allows providing custom (composite) models for `ItemStack`s.

In theory, this should be compatible with Forgified FAPI. The [`ItemRenderer` mixin](https://github.com/Sinytra/ForgifiedFabricAPI/blob/e7c57d6a9b7237f6574c7258366e4c62ad16541e/fabric-renderer-indigo/src/client/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/mixin/client/indigo/renderer/ItemRendererMixin.java#L47) appears above [NeoForge's own patch for this](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/d8d64b44bb46323d44520fe27feda0a9a08c1c82/patches/net/minecraft/client/renderer/entity/ItemRenderer.java.patch#L26), and only runs when the model is a FRAPI model.

*However*, Continuity wraps every model into a `EmissiveBakedModel`. This means that the FRAPI/Indio model rendering is always used, and so NeoForge's custom hook is not called.

## Steps to reproduce:
 1. Install the folowing mods:
    - NeoForge [21.1.248]
    - CC: Tweaked [1.120.2]
    - Continuity [3.0.0+1.21.neoforge]
    - Forgified Fabric API [0.116.15+2.3.2+1.21.1]
    - Moonlight Lib [1.21.1-3.3.3]
    - Sinytra Connector [9Bz9VtV5]
    - Supplementaries [1.21.1-3.8.9]

    I'm not quite sure why Supplementaries is required here — I don't know if its presence is needed to enable wrapping all models? I'm afraid I haven't dug too much into the code here.

 2. Open the creative menu and switch to CC:T's tab. You will observe all turtle models are missing their upgrades.

See https://github.com/cc-tweaked/CC-Tweaked/issues/2494 for more details.

The bottom edges of the path and stairs completely cover the dirt above, and it should not connect to the path between them. issues.title: Proposal: Enhance Continuity compatibility with VulkanMod / non-Indigo renderers - linked textures & overlays
issues.body:
Hi!

First off, thanks for Continuity — it's definitely among the best ways to get connected textures and emissives in OptiFine style without OptiFine. Continuity does exactly what I want: support OptiFine connected textures/emissive/custom block layers through resource packs.

However, it currently doesn't work — while running VulkanMod, a replacement renderer with Vulkan. VulkanMod replaces Minecraft's OpenGL renderer and implements its own renderer integration, including mixins and a custom rendering pipeline. It explicitly says mod compatibility isn't guaranteed and renderer-related mods can break.

VulkanMod lists Continuity under "Broken Visuals / no effect" in their own compatibility list, which matches what I'm seeing. There are also VulkanMod issues where resource packs of connected-textures cause broken visuals, and users note CTM is effectively not supported on VulkanMod right now.

Since Continuity, by design, is a feature mod for rendering/resource-pack enhancements, some of the functionality ultimately needed may require support on VulkanMod's side. However, I'd like to suggest a few changes that could improve compatibility from Continuity's side for any non-Indigo renderer implementation.

The Fabric Rendering API is designed explicitly so that model authors do not need to manipulate raw vertex data/vertex formats and should remain compatible across different renderer implementations (Indigo, Sodium's implementation, etc.), since the API hides low-level details and exposes higher-level interfaces such as RenderContext/QuadEmitter/MeshBuilder.

The documentation/architecture descriptions of VulkanMod indicate they hook rendering using mixins and provide compatibility layers and a Fabric Renderer API implementation, and FRAPI-safe integrations are the most likely path to work across renderers.

With that in mind, is it possible for Continuity to:

(1) avoid depending on Indigo-internal specifics or assumptions regarding the vanilla/Indigo pipelines, and instead use public FRAPI interfaces for overlay/connected texture emission wherever possible;

(2) add a “renderer-compat mode” that detects the VulkanMod and disables only the most incompatible features, e.g., overlays/custom block layers, while still allowing basic connected textures where possible; and/or

(3) implement a safer fallback path for connected texture selection that doesn’t depend on renderer-specific GUI/atlas blitting behavior, as the latter often gets rewritten in Vulkan renderers?

Continuity does document that it implements its own specifications for connected textures/emissive/custom block layers as extensions of OptiFine’s formats. A renderer-agnostic path there would be really helpful for pack authors and users.

Of course, I’m happy to provide the logs, resource pack examples, and test builds if you need them, but the principal “ask” here is:

Could Continuity add explicit support, or at least a graceful fallback, for VulkanMod / non-Indigo renderers by sticking strictly to FRAPI public interfaces and/or disabling conflicting render hooks when it detects VulkanMod, so the mod doesn’t become a “no effect” mod in Vulkan environments?

If the conclusion is “this must be fixed in VulkanMod,” I totally understand — but even then, guidance on what FRAPI features you need (e.g., specific material/render-layer behaviors, overlay/cutout handling) would help people report actionable compatibility requests to the maintainers of VulkanMod.

- continuity-3.0.0+1.20.5

- sodium-fabric-0.7.3+mc1.21.8.jar

issues.title: Issue with Pack Hierarchy in Overlay Handling
issues.body:
Hi,

A user of my [resource pack](https://github.com/Valdr687/Vervada-s-enhanced-plants/issues/5) encountered an issue with overlays when used alongside Overlay’s by Kany. After investigating, I found that when two packs are active simultaneously, overlays from both are enabled, rather than just the one on top.

To illustrate this, I created two test packs ([resourcepacks.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19042206/resourcepacks.zip)):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e651935-9285-4970-b29e-0b0ad2ac66ec)

In this example, one pack applies connected textures to dirt (affecting diorite), while the other affects grass blocks. As shown, the dirt connects to both, which can lead to conflicts when multiple packs have similar behaviors.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0550f83e-6d00-4cc4-a54e-841c262b9f23)

For testing, I used a minimal setup with just these two packs and the latest version of Continuity on Fabric (via Modrinth Launcher). The user who reported the issue was on Forge and shared their config in the linked issue. I’ve also observed the same behavior with OptiFine and noticed a similar report in #343.

Thanks for taking a look!

issues.title: OptiFine [suffix.emissive] property causes critical error. [Sodium + Continuity]
issues.body:
Found this by testing with [Ducky Periperals] mod:
Latest versions of Sodium and Continuity turns game font into this: [][][][][][]
Also all sounds and languages disapear from the game. Trying to enter the world results into crash.
Remowing one of the mods [Ducky Perips|Sodium|Continuity] "fixes" the problem...

The reason of the problem and actual fix:
In [duckyperiphs-1.20.1-1.3.1-fabric](https://modrinth.com/mod/ducky-periphs/version/1.20.1-1.3.1-fabric) version.
There is a file exist: `/assets/minecraft/optifine/emissive.properties` with next content: `suffix.emissive=_e`
Removing it (I removed entire `/assets/minecraft` directory) fixes the problem. All 3 mods works fine after that.

I am not sure which mod must be responsible for that, but Continuty works with OptiFine emisive textures, so I thought informing you about that might be a good idea...

issues.title: Unicode escape sequences do not work
issues.body:
Unicode escape sequences, as described [here](https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#strings) in the OptiFine documentation, do not function at all when used with Continuity; this is most notably problematic for resource packs that make extensive use of Minecraft formatting codes in block entity names to customize their appearance.

When using a standalone setup of OptiFine `HD U J3` on Minecraft `1.21.4`, block textures change as expected when Unicode escape sequences are used in their `.properties` files in a resource pack:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81785183-d4d7-46d5-b70e-79496964a1e0)

When using a Fabric setup consisting of only Continuity `3.0.0`, Fabric API `0.116.1`, Mod Menu `13.0.2`, and Text Placeholder API `2.5.2` on Minecraft `1.21.4`, textures don't change at all for the same blocks, despite having the same resource pack enabled (this also applies to other block entities, not just beacons):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4fd3942-c731-4e3e-9b9f-d394f3a6fe3d)

The resource pack I created to demonstrate this can be found here: [UnicodeTestPack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18772835/UnicodeTestPack.zip)

issues.body:
Hello! I'm not 100% sure where the origin of this bug is, as I've read through both mods mixins, and admiditly am a bit stumped as to where the issue could be stemming from, but when Continuty runs with either Better Nether or Better End (I've connfirmed that this issue doesn't happen with BClib), MinecraftClient.getInstance().world is null when the player doesn't have a screen open (inventory, furnace, pause menu, etc). I did the following tests to troubleshoot:

All results were on Fabric 0.16.10 on 1.20.1, and had Fabric API 0.92.3+1.20.1

* BClib 3.0.14
* Better End 4.0.11

* Contiuity 3.0.0+1.20.1
* BClib 3.0.14
result: works as intended

* Better End 4.0.11
result: works as intended

* BClib 3.0.14
* Better Nether 9.0.10
result: null without open screen

I also tested this in a few modpacks as well, with the same results. It only had this issue when the 2 mods were together. I learned about this issue when a mod I released had an issue rendering a custom Item that relied on the world to render a special way when both mods were present. This bug report may should instead fall onto the shader, but here's what I got my bug boiled down to:
Shader + an enchanting table resource (includes optifine-styled emissive textures) + continuity **with emissive textures on**

Minecraft 1.21.1

Fabric 0.16.10
Continuity 3.0.0+1.21 or 3.0.0-beta.5+1.21
Complementary Shaders - Reimagined r5.2.2

Iris Shaders 1.8.1+1.21.1-fabric
Sodium mc1.21.1-0.6.5-fabric

Better Enchanting Table 1.2 by Jacosvaldo 

The last piece to this enigma is that the mob emissions are dependent on what item is right-most in your hotbar. I did not test non-hotbar inventory positions. Sometimes, angle of sight / edge of your screen, or where you are rotated around mob also influences the effect.

Screenshots below show an affected mob. The item does not need to be held for this effect to activate, it just needs to be right-most in hotbar. Held to show what item was causing what effect (it's curious!). Additionally, effect is removed if F1 is pressed to hide GUI.

issues.title: Option to fall back to ctm on edges where an overlay can't be applied
issues.body:
Hi! I've looked into this quite a bit and I don't think this is something that's currently implemented. If i'm wrong, though, please feel free to correct me.
Currently, you pretty much have to "choose" between having an overlay and a CT on a face. Not literally, of course, but overlays and CTs don't interact, meaning that you're stuck these options:
1. Have overlays, but any edges without overlays will be totally bare.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bc49925-4799-4aa9-bfb1-b435b6a156d0)
2. Proper connected textures on the face, but no overlays.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/887310e6-b948-4bcf-921d-0e89a00afe2c)
3. Both overlays and connected textures, but implemented in a way that may be very undesirable in use cases like this one.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea077a7b-1b50-409d-9181-40838961425a)

With that said, I think it'd be great to have an option that "combines" CT and overlays in some way. That way, you can still have overlays while having some sort of fallback option for air or other unsupported blocks.

I'm aware that similar functionality will probably be possible in the "connection control" update, since you can just have your CT connect to the same blocks as your overlay does. However, I think a method specifically designed for this opens the door for additional features, such as custom "taper-off" tiles for overlays to transition into perpendicular CT edges:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/611cd694-0598-49ba-b8f0-d871309eef6e)

I'm not sure if this would be overly complicated or even impossible with however CTM and overlay are implemented, but I figured it'd be worth it to ask. Would be a game changer for stylized resource packs where outlines are very important to define edges of blocks.

issues.body:

I have allocated 32gb of ram out of 64gb to the game, using a 13th gen i9 KF and a 12gb rtx 3060 if this helps.

issues.title: Glass connecting shows incorrect textures. [1.21 Fabric]
issues.body:
I was playing my testing world when I logged out of the world to do something else. When I logged back into the world, I didn't see anything else wrong until I got out of what was going to be my slime farm. I used lime green glass to make a slime out of blocks, but when I went to go mess with the design, the blocks looked like parts of chests and shulker boxes! I later tested this for the other glass types and discovered that most, if not all of the other glass types had this same issue. Some, the regular glass in particular, didn't show up at all, even with nothing placed next to the glass. The issue itself is evident when placing down just one block of any glass type.

All the mods I have mostly follow the Fabulously Optimized mod pack's beta 1.21 version with my personal additions of Journey Map, JEI, Clumps, Jade, Leaves Be Gone, and Not Enough Animations. I have had these mods along with continuity before and no problems had occurred to my knowledge before, so this is the first time this has occurred for me. I hope this helps solve the issue.

issues.title: Falling block crashes Minecraft
issues.body:
# Overview

With Continuity 3.0.0-beta.5+1.21, rendering any falling blocks, including but not limited to falling sand, falling red sand, falling gravel, falling concrete powder, will crash the game.

# Steps to reproduce

## Version 1: naturally generated falling block

1. Launch Minecraft with Continuity mod and Fabric API.
2. Create a world.
3. If there's any naturally generated falling block being rendered, your minecraft crashes.

## Version 2: manually placed falling block

1. Launch Minecraft with Continuity mod and Fabric API.
2. Create a world. If you're lucky, no naturally generated falling block will be rendered yet and your Minecraft will not crash.
3. Place a block of sand/red sand/gravel/concrete powder several blocks above the ground and let it fall.
4. Alternately, you can /summon any falling block above the ground and let it fall.
5. Minecraft renders the falling block and crashes.

# Crash reports and logs

Crash report (naturally generated falling block): 
[crash-2024-07-10_17.10.11-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16158545/crash-2024-07-10_17.10.11-client.txt)

[crash-2024-07-10_17.03.53-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16158577/crash-2024-07-10_17.03.53-client.txt)

(I don't think these two many any differences in terms of crash mechanics but whatever)

issues.title: (Enhancement) Support for overlays for blocks with different position on 2 axis
issues.body:
Currently CT only works when the blocks are off by 1 block on 1 axis (ie. their faces are parallel to each other)

It would be great if CT could be made to work even on blocks which are off by 1 block on 2 axis (ie. their faces are perpendicular to each other). This should require the RSP to inform the mod if a particular CT should apply to perpenducular blocks as it probably wouldn't always be desirable. This also means this new feature wouldn't retroactively change the look of CT texture packs.

This be a big feature but it would easily make continuity the best connected textures mod out there as none other have this. 
Ik you're not exactly planning on adding such things rn but if you ever consider adding more features beyond what optifine has this'd be great

issues.title: Held Enchanted Items Glitched in Inventory - 1.20.4
issues.body:
On the hotbar they look fine. 
In the game itself they are fine.

Held in Inventory view they are blown out and glitched.

![MC Continuity Distortion](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/123700111/3d7165eb-0a5d-4a64-b569-e1c4205320bb)

After some testing, it turns out that this happens so long as any texture pack that uses emissive textures is enabled.
I am using Ozocraft Remix as a texture pack (which uses emissive), and Visible Ores. The latter is the reason I wanted to install Continuity for 1.20.4 in Fabric.

Taking Ozocraft Remix out and Visible Ores, it behaves as usual. Adding either of them back seems to bork the rendering of enchanted items in hand for Inventory. That being said there is no reason Visible Ores should affect enchanted held items, and yet it does. This brings me to conclude the glitch has something to do with this version of Continuity and the moment the portion for activating Emissive textures comes into play, bringing that glitch on.

![MC Continuity Distortion - MODS](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/123700111/938e1eee-35f4-4b32-b39b-b46f795b118f)

I'm not running a lot of mods, either, and have effectively removed all unneeded mods to test.
The glitch only seems to appear when emissive textures are present in the texturepack in any form.

issues.title: Continuity crashing when opening inventory (1.21 Fabric)
issues.body:
The game crashes 100% of the time I open my inventory but only when holding an enchanted item. I believe people have already ran into a similar issue like this for the past few years, but I don't see them providing specific details.

Here's some details that I tried my best to narrow down where the issue could be:

- Crash ONLY happens specifically when opening inventory and holding an enchanted item in your hand, either main or offhand.
- Crash ONLY happens when emissive lighting is enabled in Continuity settings.
- Crashes ONLY when using any resource pack that has emissive textures.
- Crashes whether or not shaders are enabled or disabled, but if Iris is kept installed.
- Does not crash when Iris is removed.
- Does not crash when only using default resource pack.
- Does not crash when not holding an enchanted item (or any item with the enchanted glint)
- Does not crash when continuity is disabled or removed from mods folder.

Mods and crash report attached below

issues.title: Overlay textures don't work on non-full blocks
issues.body:
Overlay-type connected textures (specifically `overlay_fixed` in my case) do not appear to work on non-full blocks. Here I am attempting to make mossy cobblestone colored based on the biome via `matchTiles`; this works fine for the regular block, but not for stairs, slabs, or walls, which end up rendering either a singular floating copy of the overlay above the block or nothing at all.

issues.title: Blocks are rendered without offset
issues.body:
So idk how and idk why but when Continuity AND a texture pack that uses connected textures (any) is on, any block that is rendered with the following code does NOT follow what vanilla does as the block is rendered at the center instead of using its Offset. 
 ` 
       blockRenderer.getModelRenderer().tesselateBlock(level, blockRenderer.getBlockModel(state), state, pos, poseStack, buffer.getBuffer(ItemBlockRenderTypes.getMovingBlockRenderType(state)),
                false, RandomSource.create(), seed, OverlayTexture.NO_OVERLAY);
 ` 

As a consequence, when those 2 conditions are there, my mod, A Good Place, displays an erroneus animation for the block. This took me ages to figure out as it also needed that texture pack to be on (was a random pack that just altered leaves)

3.0.0-beta+4 (both Instances)
### Hephaestus Version
3.6.3.232 (both Instances)

### Issue(s)
Whenever loading both Continuity and Hephaestus together, any items from Hephaestus end up rendering invisible in Hephaestus' blocks—namely the Casting Basin and Casting Table. Fluids are also all white, even if they have different colors to signify different smelted ore types, and are also rendered invisible when pouring into a Basin or Table. Particle effects work fine (casted parts and ingots sizzle and blow little black particles to signify they're finished cooling).

Disabling Continuity fixes the issue completely, and the reverse—disabling Hephaestus fixes the issue with resource packs requiring Continuity to continue working. I hope that makes sense, I am very tired from handing out candy today! Using Fabric over Quilt also doesn't fix either issue —they still persist, so I don't think it's a problem with the loader itself. I included both loader versions because I did testing between both of them, so maybe it will help.

### More Info/Other Stuff
I found out the incompatibility through brute force. I kept getting invisible items and went through my mod list one by one (it's quite big, almost modpack size, but all of the mods work just fine together, no problems!) and found out that it was indeed Continuity causing both issues. I don't know if it's an incompatibility on Hephaestus' end or this one, so I figured I would open a bug report here in case the incompatibility is not intentional and can at all be fixed and is on Continuity's end instead of Hephaestus'. 

Similarly, I had already opened a bug report on Hephaestus' side of things in case the issue is on that side. I should have made the bug report here yesterday, but I was exhausted and had to sleep to be ready for today. That's totally on me and I apologize!

### Minecraft Log and Hephaestus' bug report
[here is my Minecraft log](https://pastebin.com/AnfAgyRW) with Continuity _and_ Hephaestus enabled; I hope it's of some help! [Here is also the report on Hephaestus' end](https://github.com/Alpha-s-Stuff/TinkersConstruct/issues/85), which is a little more in-depth but a little roundabout as I did not realize it was Continuity at first (I thought it was Quilt; this is now not true, and I apologize for the jumbled mess there and also here).

DirTNT / stitch compatibility
issues.body:
Hey, DirTNT dev here!
I've written an internal texture stitching library named stitch to dynamically generate / add textures based of other textures, so I can generate TNT textures for potentially every possible block in the game.

Afaik older Continuity versions run fine with DirTNT/stitch, but compatibility broke with the 3.0.0 beta, see https://github.com/Fourmisain/DirTNT/issues/5.
Here's the relevant excerpt:
> java.lang.ClassCastException: class io.github.fourmisain.stitch.impl.StitchImpl$SpritesStage cannot be cast to class net.minecraft.class_7766$class_7767 (io.github.fourmisain.stitch.impl.StitchImpl$SpritesStage and net.minecraft.class_7766$class_7767 are in unnamed module of loader net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassLoader @5cb9f472)
	at net.minecraft.class_7766.mdb6f098$continuity$lambda$continuity$modifyFunction$4$7(class_7766.java:1090) ~[client-intermediary.jar:?]
	... 9 more

It looks like one of your mixins expects `class_7766$class_7767` aka `SpriteLoader$StitchResult`, but instead gets my custom `SpritesStage`.

Due to the way the texture stitching stages are threaded, it wasn't easy finding a way to transfer data from one stage to another and to extend the stitching process without potential deadlocks or using a separate thread pool. The "best" solution I could come up with was to use a horrible `@Overwrite` to add [2 new stages to the stitching process](https://github.com/Fourmisain/DirTNT/blob/ea7f24283d716faad335279d43b55b491ee37e4a/stitch/src/main/java/io/github/fourmisain/stitch/mixin/SpriteLoaderMixin.java#L39-L51).
`prepareGenerating()` is what returns our lovely `SpritesStage`.

I'm not actually sure how your mixin catches that, since the quoted code should be all `SpritesStage` is used for.
I assume you might have an injector targeting some lambda/s inside `load`?
Maybe they could target the internally called methods like `loadAll` / `stitch` instead?
Or maybe a solution could be as easy as adding an `instanceof SpriteLoader$StitchResult` check?
I'd try to look into it myself, but this repo's source code only goes up to the last 1.19.2 version.
Can you push your beta code to a separate branch maybe?

Thanks and sorry for the wall of text... 😅

issues.title: Remove render layer limitations in block.properties
issues.body: It's impossible to change the render layer of many blocks via block.properties, presumably to make x-raying more difficult. This is, however, ultimately redundant due to the fact that many other resource pack methods can be used to achieve the same effect (e.g. replacing the models of certain blocks, or retexturing some blocks such as grass blocks which already use cutout rendering and themselves cull solid blocks). For the sake of creative liberty, it might be advisable to lift these restrictions - if someone is willing to install a mod that allows for extra texture pack customizability in order to exploit block.properties, they could just as easily install a mod or vanilla resource pack that grants them an unfair advantage anyway.

issues.title: Better glass pane connected textures by fixing vanilla model issues
issues.body:
Currently, glass pane connected textures simply leave the vanilla glass pane model unchanged, and cause every part that uses the glass texture to be connected as a full glass block would. This exaggerates several of the incongruities that exist in vanilla, which is not a desirable outcome. For example, it's common to see edges of panes abruptly ending and seamlessly blending into the background, when you'd expect a border of pixels there. Vertical pillars of single panes also look *completely* invisible with modern textures, save for the very bottom and top.

With a bit of model reworking and CTM magic, we can get rid of almost all of these issues and achieve a much nicer looking result - we get a border at just about every edge where it'd be expected where previously absent, a massive improvement over what we currently have.

Current CTM appearance:
![2023-08-12_20 27 19](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/179f52c4-a6c1-4699-a053-ed4112835213)

Fixed:
![2023-08-12_20 27 04](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/575665bb-0397-4a8e-a9e7-438efe074349)

The only things stopping this from being a complete fix are #74 and #295 - if these are addressed, a perfect set of models should be completely achievable.

Here's a downloadable demonstration of the best that can be achieved for panes so far:
[pane-fix-demo-v1.0.zip](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/files/12328168/pane-fix-demo-v1.0.zip)

Only normal glass panes in the default textures are fixed by this resource pack - Programmer Art and stained glass panes are completely unaffected. If this idea is approved, I can work on the required textures and models to bring this to all pane colors across both packs.

My idea is that this would be offered with the mod as a third built-in resource pack alongside the current two. Since it redoes the vanilla models, the culling "fix" is present in this pack by default.

issues.title: Better vertical CTM control for glass panes
issues.body:
This arrangement of glass panes:
![2023-08-06_01 44 47](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/0f8d2569-3375-4a54-b8bc-0df6a8c17069)

looks like this with CTM enabled:
![2023-08-06_01 44 34](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/63dd61ac-c981-4860-a5a6-a913230216c0)

There's a nice continuous border around the edges of the glass for the most part, but it terminates at two points.
![doctored](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/95be70a8-39ec-4222-a7fa-b8c14474c6d5)

The blue border is probably very easy to fix with model files alone and specific CTM for this texture (I myself have fixed this in a non-CTM context by redoing the models), but the red line would require that the pane should not only detect the presence of a glass pane above or below it, but also its connection type. To my knowledge, the mod does not currently allow for this.

Even OptiFine, with its #74 fix, is not immune to this problem, with textures connecting in sub-block places where they really should not:
![2023-08-06_02 00 50](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/assets/52297970/f0c77a12-d0f4-4437-b110-6ec43995c797)

I don't really know how complicated a fix for this would be, but it's something I'd like to see quite a lot since a fix for it and #74 would allow for absolutely perfect glass pane connections.

issues.title: Conflict between connected grass and blocks overlays
issues.body:
Minecraft version 1.19.4
Continuity version: 3.0.0-beta.2+1.19.3
Indium: 1.0.15+mc1.19.4
Packs used: xali's Enhanced Vanilla + Continuity built-in better grass

Issue:
The overlay of some of the blocks don't work at all when using the built-in better grass.
Expected result (as seen in Optifine):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5339303/235667600-c917c2de-a577-4540-9b79-791afaff8ef3.png)
Has both the better grass with the sides, and the overlay on the dirt path

Current result: (with Sodium, Continuity, Indium)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5339303/235664037-4b637368-6205-4e47-ab23-ae9c064e0a85.png)
Has no overlay if better grass is activated
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5339303/235666308-e6b9294c-8546-49fe-9f83-2ab4f6adf2ad.png)
Has overlay if better grass isn't activated

I tried using the mods with both possible orders (BG above Xali, and Xali above BG), both result in the same bug, although putting Xali above has some of the corners overlay appear, but seemingly at random.
I figured the effect was with Continuity since having the shaders on or off changes nothing to the issue.

have a nice day everyone.

issues.title: Configuration for how blocks interact with water rendering?
issues.body:
In vanilla, certain blocks will render differently around water, and water will render differently around them: the dowwards flowing water texture will not be rendered from within the water, and will be replaced with a single, solid color texture from the other side.

In vanilla, glass interacts with water in this way, but beacons do not. In the following screenshots, I've assigned the same model to glass and beacons. The blocks that don't have the blue water overlay are glass, and the ones that do are beacons.
![2023-04-14_16 47 51](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/232094544-f6e94324-e3fe-48ff-b818-033ab0a0bc7c.png)

I'm not sure if this would fit in the scope of the mod or would be possible to implement in the first place, but it does get in the way of my goal to have glass and beacons connect to each other seamlessly (like #242 and the second issue I highlighted in #241), so this seemed like the most fitting place to report it.

I do know that Sodium does appear to touch water rendering to some extent resulting in deviations from vanilla (https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/991, which is unrelated to https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/38 but that issue can be seen here as well): 
![2023-04-14_16 53 33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/232095138-09c74fe2-9b73-4ece-9d01-d2de429b690d.png)

issues.title: Tripwire rendering type as a selectable option in block.properties?
issues.body:
In vanilla, there are two different rendering types used for rendering translucent blocks in the world according to the wiki's "shaders" page: there's "rendertype_translucent" used by water, ice, slime blocks, honey blocks, tinted glass, stained glass and its panes, and nether portals, and there's "rendertype_tripwire" which is used exclusively by tripwire.

I'm not sure if making tripwire an option that certain blocks can use via block.properties would be possible at all since I don't know if there exists a distinction between a "rendertype" and a "block layer".

The behaviour of rendertype_tripwire is quite strange - I've reported https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-261837 to keep track of it. It appears that from some angles, it occludes all other tripwire blocks behind it, like how translucent blocks rendered before release 1.7, but from other angles, no culling happens at all.

issues.title: Configuration for culling certain faces?
issues.body:
Yet another Hollow Glass Saga observation: it's possible for some planes to start z-fighting with the custom model I'm using. Some way to override what blocks can cull against other blocks using a resource pack might be useful to get rid of this effect. I'm not sure if this would be at all possible to implement here, though.
![2023-04-10_12 49 54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/230898548-cd3cc21e-7d47-4a10-88c0-26cc8ae616e0.png)

More significantly, there's a vanilla issue with beacons. The vanilla beacon model doesn't specify cullface for anything ([MC-239142](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-239142)). However, even if we do turn it on for the outer planes, for example, beacons still won't cull against other beacons. They also won't cull against glass blocks, nor will glass blocks cull against beacons. This results in many inner planes which are already a pain in vanilla, and become even more of a menace if you're trying to do CTM to make beacons connect with each other in a good-looking way. If there exists some way for a resource pack to say "beacons cull against beacons, beacons cull against glass, and glass culls against beacons", that would allow for this issue to be resolved. I don't know if that's doable.

issues.title: [Request] innerSeams against other blocks?
issues.body:
Today I've been experimenting with MCPatcher's CTM functionality to see if I could backport the WIP resource pack I'll never complete back to then, and to understand the differences between historical and modern implementations of connected textures (such as things mentioned in #231). There's one thing I've noticed about innerSeams back then: they would apply against any full blocks which obstructed a face, rather than only instances of the same block.

Here's a screenshot using the experimental pack in 1.7.10. This is how it looks with innerSeams disabled:
![2023-04-01_15 33 05](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296514-d8e513b1-abdf-438e-a131-c72a7d97589d.png)
![2023-04-01_15 33 06](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296516-5af3e534-efef-4ff4-8aa4-53d1c9c8c2d1.png)

And with it enabled:
![2023-04-01_15 33 26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296525-524d7841-c46b-48d5-b821-50a91153d4b3.png)
![2023-04-01_15 33 27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296527-f0e97a6d-12b1-48ad-8063-b106c1a0ed1f.png)

With Continuity in 1.19.4, even if innerSeams is enabled, blocks of other types will not cause this effect to happen.
![2023-04-01_15 47 41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296555-912a9e4d-cc9a-4cc5-abbe-ccaaeb7d874b.png)

The same is true in OptiFine (so I may also open a request there):
![2023-04-01_15 41 54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/229296566-01909196-7b40-4f70-9605-f9a7f0f54aec.png)

Of course, just changing the current innerSeams behaviour to this one from 1.7.10 would be undesirable since many resource packs are built under the assumption of the current behaviour. However, I think I personally prefer the MCPatcher handling of cases like these. Would an option of some sort be possible that could allow for changes between these two different types of innerSeams behaviour (current "only against same block type" behaviour would be default, and there'd be a second "against any block that culls the face of this block" option), assuming it doesn't exist already? I'm not sure if this would fit entirely in the scope of the mod if it's only meant to be compatible with OptiFine's CTM implementation, but it's something I'd very much like to see if possible.

I can provide the resource packs used in each case if desired for testing purposes.

Currently developing a resource pack which contains a custom model for glass blocks containing inner faces. I've attached minimal resource packs containing these models for testing.

When innerSeams is not enabled, the back faces of pretty much any shape constructed from glass blocks render connected like the front faces do.
![2023-03-30_07 13 30](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52297970/228749134-9d0a1454-c7ee-44f6-9754-0b9ab16fceda.png)

The two test resource packs can be found as follows:

After some testing, it turned out that the Continuity mod on 1.18.2 is causing wild problems for the optifine texture fusion system of the popular Conquest resource pack.

issues.title: Performance tanks when "Emissive Textures" is enabled (details inside)
issues.body:
So this is a bit of a weird one. To recreate the scenario, you need:

1) a version of Minecraft with the Fabric mod loader
2) a resource pack that offers optifine-style emissive item textures, such as John Smith Legacy
3) Continuity installed and either A) [Model Gap Fix](https://modrinth.com/mod/modelfix) or B) [Item Model Fix](https://modrinth.com/mod/item-model-fix) set to the "Pixel" fix option.

For reasons I don't quite understand, items that have emissive textures result in a **massive** performance drop when the two aforementioned mods are used, and Continuity has "Emissive Textures" on. 

Example of a chest with some random items:

![216037011-974b2dfe-7247-4dde-8a70-34727cedb530](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11655762/216139006-a2416aad-1da5-456e-9f8e-ebca9b4e6d8c.png)

And another chest with a bunch of lava buckets, which use an emissive texture, even though it's basically useless as an inventory item preview. For reference though, the lag occurs so long as the item's icon shows anywhere, be it in an inventory, held on hand, or dropped and floating on the ground somewhere:

![216037082-46ff84dc-8b12-4c3c-8eec-e4fe87283846](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11655762/216139024-b5ae5d56-f5db-49c1-9e41-81931e2f1e03.png)

Disabling the "Emissive Textures" option in Continuity sees the framerate from either mod drop equally, though nowhere near as bad as when it was on previously. I have not tested whether the same situation occurs in Forge with Optifine to be 100% sure that this is Continuity, but then again I find it rather improbably that two independent mod makers made the exact same mistake that'd cause this big a loss in performance.

issues.title: overlay_compact
issues.body:
It could be an easy way to create overlays for blocks. Of course it would not work for every blocks but it could reduce the amount of texture a bunch for some blocks.
It would require to get rotated textures for overlays but by doing so, it could be possible to use significantly less textures. I'm guessing it is possible to use only part of a texture for doing this. 

Using only 3 textures, you could have 
One texture for block that are surrounded
One texture for x and y overlays. It would make it more useful for texture like planks logs
One texture that would be both corners. 

Here is a little template I made as an example
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2474569/196236114-6dcaf8c4-47f9-4877-82eb-de716facc3b6.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2474569/196236759-3083aeb1-90ca-4d5e-9888-efc7c6f338bc.png)

I don't know how efficient this could be but I'll let you be the judge.

issues.title: Textures Not Connecting In 1.19
issues.body:
So I recently followed a tutorial on how to setup connected textures for Iris, because that was the one feature from Optifine I greatly missed. Upon opening up the game, all the mods I was told to installed were properly there (namely: Continuity, Iridium, Iris, Mods Menu, and Sodium). However, once entering a world the textures were not connecting. I checked the options in the mod menu for Continuity and all of them were properly set to connect the game's textures.

I have attached a list of the mods my latest log includes, if any other information is needed that I am leaving out just let me know.
[listOfLoggedMods.txt](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/files/9277663/listOfLoggedMods.txt)

issues.title: Crashes with Sodium/BetterNether
issues.body:
We are currently having an issue with a crash related to Continuity, Sodium and BetterNether (quiqueck/BetterNether#3).
I've done some simple testing (mainly disabling our custom emissive material and model loader code), but the error seems to persist. However, to move forward I would need a little help.

It seems that this static initializer is called before the fabric renderer is ready:
https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/blob/9686d62bde4311ad9b0fd974dbeaf57135e311cc/src/main/java/me/pepperbell/continuity/client/util/RenderUtil.java#L38

If BetterNether is causing this error, you may be able to track down the call that triggers the initialization in the debugger. But it may not be related to BetterNether at all, as the crash also goes away when removing Sodium.

The minimum ste of Mods required to reproduce the issue is:
- bclib 2.0.1
- betternether 7.0.1
- continuity 2.0.0+1.19
- sodium 0.4.2+build.16

issues.title: [incompatible] Dashloader (half compatible)
issues.body:
** The Problem**
this will half work when dashloader takes its first cache this will work fine and nothing will seem wrong, its only on resource reload dashloader seems to break this mod and any blocks this mod has touched. I think I understand why this is a thing.


** Possible work around**
hook into dashloader (it has a API) on resource reload events and remove its cache to force dashloader to re-cache everything properly i worked with another dev who just delete the cache directly (config/QuantumFusion/Dashloader) then allow the resource reload to continue

issues.title: Repeat method not working correctly
issues.body:
**MC** 1.17.1
**Continuity** 1.0.0

1. Install Continuity
2. Install [NAPP](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/napp-free-version-1-01) and/or [FJGlass](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/faithful-jappa-ctm-glass) texture packs
3. Install [Lambdabettergrass](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/lambdabettergrass) and activate its resource pack (I know, this one is not an optifine TP, but it's needed for the example testing)

Expected result: all textures connect as intended.

Actual result: if only NAPP is installed and Continuity resource packs are loaded and placed below it, only glass and glass panes connect; if Continuity packs are disabled or placed above NAPP then no textures connect; if FJGlass is installed and placed above NAPP, glass and glass panes also do not connect; Lambdabettergrass works and connects as inteded in all cases.

There's another connected textures mod - [ConnectedBlockTextures](https://github.com/HyperCubeMC/connected-block-textures). With it installed instead of Continuity, all NAPP textures connect, except for glass and glass panes; if FJGlass is installed, then glass and glass panes also connect. Lambdabettergrass does not work, no grass textures are connected.

What am I doing wrong?
